known_limitations: No event engine (by design, lane G owns it): scenarios use direct calls + qmint.classical.common.deliver/path_delay_ns; _run_chain in scenarios.py follows a single request/response chain in time order and should be replaced by G's engine when available.
All latencies are lightcone lower bounds on SYNTHETIC networks; no fiber, queueing, RIPE data.
H2: steady-state leader only; no leader election/view change, crash faults only (no Byzantine), no cross-shard txns; conflicting in-flight spend rejected conservatively.
H3 late_commit_ot_private uses an IDEAL OT functionality; real OT instantiation NOT_IMPLEMENTED and necessarily computational.
H4 timings from pure-Python reference ML-DSA (dilithium_py README: not secure, educational); liboqs not installed.
H5 is a trust model; HMAC stands in for asymmetric device attestation; no real device benchmarked.

H6: toy 512-bit RSA; SHA-256 for f,g (g not bijective => untraceability heuristic, not unconditional); CFN Sec.2 (framing protection) and Sec.3 not implemented; colluding merchants with identical challenges defeat tracing (paper notes this).
H6 source read from a Wayback archive copy, not the Springer original.
pqc timings are embedded in H4 record configuration, so H4 record_ids change between runs.
interfaces_changed: None to frozen contracts. Proposal for lane G: host nodes satisfying qmint.classical.common.ProtocolNode (node_id, site_id, processing_ns, handle(Message, now_ns)->list[Message]); MerchantTerminal.on_timeout(idem_key, now_ns) needs a timer hook.
